A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NEP/RLlamaGen research, with readable text, equations, figures and tables. The complete documents were inspected: v1 ends with references, while v2 additionally includes a NeurIPS checklist rather than a scientific appendix.

before.justification: Sections 3.2-3.4 report original image-editing evaluations, ablations, computational measurements, text-to-image generation results and test-time refinement experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds quantitative zero-shot editing comparisons, generation-order results and qualitative mask-conditioning ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3.3.1 revises the stated zero-shot inference procedure: v1 describes removing edited-region tokens before regeneration, whereas v2 explicitly describes keeping all source-image tokens visible. This changes the reported conditioning procedure; the core two-stage architecture, mask embeddings and equations remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish an implementation change or rerunning of retained results.

E1.justification: The training sources and MagicBrush, Emu Edit and MS-COCO evaluation coverage are retained. The new quantitative experiments concern already-present zero-shot local editing on MagicBrush, without introducing another dataset, domain or task requirement. Noisy masks are discussed but not newly tested.

E2.justification: v2 adds aMUSEd as an evaluated zero-shot editing comparator in Table 5. Comparator membership in the retained editing, efficiency and text-to-image comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds a controlled comparison of in-mask random versus raster generation orders and a quantitative zero-shot comparison using MagicBrush's single-turn and multi-turn settings. The existing experiments retain their metrics, training budgets, model size and resolution settings.

E4.justification: New Table 6 tests sensitivity to generation order, while new Figure 3 provides four cases illustrating failure to edit when editing-region conditioning is removed. The original numerical conditioning and NEP-versus-NTP ablations remain unchanged. The expanded mask-noise discussion supplies no dedicated robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. v2's checklist explicitly acknowledges the absence of significance testing, without changing the statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Retained Tables 1-4 and v1 Table 5, renumbered Table 7 in v2, have unchanged numerical results. New Tables 5-6 report zero-shot comparisons and near-matching generation-order results. For example, the zero-shot model beats aMUSEd on single-turn L1, 0.0743 versus 0.0913, but trails on multi-turn DINO, 0.7859 versus 0.8092.

T1.justification: The autoregressive factorizations and mask-token definitions in Equations (1)-(4) are unchanged. No formal assumptions, theoretical results or proofs are added; the positional-embedding annotations explain existing mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: localized token regeneration, two-stage random-order pretraining and editing, competitive editing performance, and iterative test-time scaling. The added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 attributes its aMUSEd comparison results to source-token visibility and interprets the order ablation as robustness to generation order. Section 6 adds specific discussion of oversized and undersized editing masks, acknowledging missing optimization for undersized masks. Its oversized-mask argument draws on existing free-form results rather than a new mask-noise test.

D1.justification: v2 identifies CLIP-ViT-B/32 as the critic and ImageReward as the reward model, specifies using aMUSEd's public checkpoint and default configuration, and adds an explicit code-release promise in the checklist. These improve disclosure; existing training details are retained, and the PDFs do not establish actual code availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to RandAR and aMUSEd, acknowledging another random-order generation approach and positioning zero-shot editing against aMUSEd. The existing related-work discussion and broader research positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds localized explanatory paragraphs, introduces the ERC abbreviation, expands limitations, updates the author and affiliation block, and appends a NeurIPS checklist. The scientific section sequence and most existing prose are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 3 and Tables 5-6, annotates Figure 2 with positional embeddings, and reformats the title page and several tables. Existing qualitative figures and the pretraining/refinement table are retained with relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the previously qualitative zero-shot evaluation with a comparator and generation-order check, adds informative conditioning-ablation examples, and documents more specific limitations and implementation choices. These are useful but limited gains. Statistical uncertainty remains absent, aMUSEd's better multi-turn DINO score qualifies the superiority wording, and the revised zero-shot conditioning description is not explained.
